To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spectral form factor is a function of the eigenfunction correlation function, which can be calculated from a Langevin equation that is a Brownian motion of the random walk ensemble.
The spectral statistics of disordered systems are related to wavefunction correlations by a Brownian-motion model for the energy levels.
the spectral form factor of a metal can be obtained by solving a Langevin equation for fictitious time, and the Langevin equation relates eigenfunction correlations to spectral statistics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the statistical properties of the electronic energy levels in disorganized conductors.
the statistical properties of quantum systems, and their connection with classical dynamics.
the statistical analysis of the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of large random matrices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory of quantum chaos is still in its infancy.
the spectral correlations in the disordered metal are determined by the wavefunction correlations.
the random matrix theory of disordered conductors is a theory of wave-function correlations in the limit of strong disorder, rather than of level statistics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the random walk through the ensemble of random potentials can be viewed as a Brownian motion in the space of the energy levels.
the random walk model provides a natural framework to understand the interrelation between the spectral statistics and the eigenfunction correlations in disordered metals.
we show the spectral statistics and eigenfunction correlations of disordered metals are linked through a Langevin equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spectral form factor is a universal function of the ensemble-average of the eigenfunction correlation function, and is therefore independent of the microscopic details of the disorder.
spectral statistics can be understood as a consequence of the wave-function structure in a disordered metal.
the spectral form factor is determined by the ensemble average of the square of the overlap integral between two eigenfunctions.
